text:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency_sla_breach detected in us-east-1-prod. p95 ~ 2.1s, p99 spiking to ~12s for streaming endpoints. Affected service: inference-streamer.
marco (oncall): I'm on it. paging channel and starting initial triage.
alice: seeing correlated increase in KV cache misses and a rise in GPU ECC correctables in the node pool stats.
jun: which node pool? any AZ skew?
alice: us-east-1a, pool=gpu-pool-3. Nodes: gpunode-13, gpunode-14 show elevated ECC counts. gpunode-13 temp ~86C.
marco (oncall): good, marking as P1. @karen (product) heads-up — some customer streams may be experiencing stalls.
karen (product): thanks. which customers are hitting this? support-bot: querying request traces now...
support-bot: top affected tenants: acct-104, acct-271, acct-999. ~8% of total streaming requests seeing >5s tail, 2% >10s.
dmitri: logs show repeated kv cache eviction + streaming stall loop around requests that hit cold kv. suspect the GPU node is intermittently dropping packets/IO causing stall.
ops-bot: auto-remediation attempted: scaled fallback pool + routed 20% traffic to dedicated-fallback-model, no change in p99.
marco (oncall): action plan: 1) isolate suspected hardware node 2) drain gpunode-13 from serving 3) route new sessions away 4) keep canary traffic on older model variant if necessary.
alice: running quick probe: ssh into gpunode-13, grabbing dmesg and nvml stats.
--- logs ---
[  1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00.0: Corrected ECC error detected.
NVML: ecc.correctable_count=57, temp=86.1C, perf_state=P0
streamer: stall_detected: request_id=xyz-143, stall_ms=7200
----------------
jun: that ECC count jumped quickly over last 10m. can we repro with a synthetic workload?
marco (oncall): not yet. set up a low-volume synthetic to the node via debug pool, but avoid customer impact.
marco (oncall): draining gpunode-13 now:
```
kubectl cordon node/gpunode-13
kubectl drain node/gpunode-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
marco (oncall): draining — moving current sessions out. monitoring p99.
alice: draining logs show a couple of stuck streaming sessions that did not gracefully reconnect, likely due to in-flight KV state. i'll force-fail them to let clients reconnect.
marco (oncall): forced disconnect for stuck sessions.
support-bot: reconnect rates normalizing, but p99 still elevated at ~6.5s.
dmitri: after drain started, gpunode-14 shows a small uptick in ECCs too. could be rack-level thermal issue or shared PSU.
marco (oncall): ops-bot, can you spin up replacement nodes in us-east-1a and move traffic?
ops-bot: launching replacement instances (type: a100-40gb-q). provisioning ETA ~5m.
marco (oncall): temporary mitigation: enable strict-kv-cache-ttl to reduce cold miss storms and route 40% streaming traffic to cpu-fallback pool.
alice: TTL tweak applied: kv_cache.ttl=30s for streaming route.
support-bot: customer impact update: timeouts dropped by 60% for acct-104, overall error rate trending down.
karen (product): keep me posted — customers on chat are asking for ETA. we'll prepare a brief note.
jun: suggest we also collect NVMe/ecc counters for the entire rack and open a hardware ticket in parallel.
marco (oncall): agreed. created hardware ticket HT-5421, escalated to data center engineering. attaching dmesg and nvml output.
marco (oncall): current status: drained gpunode-13, replaced nodes coming up, p99 down to ~2.8s but streaming stalls still observed sporadically (p99 tailish).
dmitri: hypothesis: intermittent I/O path saturation on the rack switch causing retry loops in our NVMe-over-fabric -> that increases stall detection in streamer and cascades to p99.
alice: running a cross-check: switch errors on tor-switch-12: rx_errors=230, tx_errors=210 in last 15m.
marco (oncall): good catch. ops-bot, can we divert traffic off that TOR to TOR-13?
ops-bot: re-routing in progress via BGP community (low-impact) — change applied.
marco (oncall): monitor p99 after reroute.
support-bot: immediate improvement: p99 fell from 2.8s to 1.6s for streaming routes, residual stalls rare.
karen (product): ok please hold for 30m then send a customer-facing incident summary. prep a concise statement: cause, mitigation, impact, ETA for full postmortem.
marco (oncall): will do. open items: 1) hardware follow-up on gpunode-13/tor-switch-12 2) validate ECC thresholds and auto-evacuate policy 3) add stronger streamer retry backoff to avoid stall amplification.
jun: I'll own ECC threshold tuning and add a guard to auto-evacuate node at correctable_count>30 within 10m.
alice: I'll open a tracing eval to see if any request pattern increases cold KV pressure — might help Optimize team tune batching.
dmitri: recommend we add a synthetic job to exercise KV hot path and thermal stress nightly to catch early regression.
marco (oncall): handing off to next oncall (alice) in 5m for cleanup and post-incident notes. final status: mitigated, partial customer impact (brief streaming stalls for ~35 minutes affecting ~8% of streaming traffic, most resolved after TOR reroute and node drain).
karen (product): thanks, team. we'll coordinate comms.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigation deployed). Severity: P1->P0. Postmortem due EOD + 48h follow-up on hardware ticket.
marco (oncall): adding action items to #postmortems and notifying infra leads. good job everyone. :thumbsup:
